title: Phone and appointments
description: Make and answer phone calls, ask for someone, and fix a time to meet.

guide.title: On the phone
guide.text:
'To phone' is fon maadu, literally 'do phone'; many people also say kaal maadu. 'To message' is mesej maadu. The person you call is in the dative: nimage fon maadteeni, 'I'll call you'.

A call begins with ಹಲೋ (halo). To ask who is calling: yaaru maataadtirodu? - 'who (is it that is) speaking?'. maataadtirodu is the spoken verbal noun 'the one speaking'; the written form is ಮಾತಾಡುತ್ತಿರುವುದು (maataaduttiruvudu).

To say who you are: naanu ravi maataadtiddeeni, 'I Ravi am-speaking'.

When the line is bad: ಕೇಳಿಸ್ತಿಲ್ಲ (kelistilla), 'it is not audible' = 'I can't hear you'; svalpa joraagi maataadi, 'speak a little louder'. kelisu means 'to be heard'; kelistide is 'I can hear you'.

To end a call people say fon idteeni, 'I'll put the phone down', or simply sari, sigona.

guide.title: Asking for someone
guide.text:
To ask whether someone is there, use the respectful plural of iru with the question ending: ravi iddaaraa? 'Is Ravi there?'. Adding ಅವರು (avaru) after a name is the polite equivalent of Mr or Ms: ravi avaru iddaaraa?

Possible answers: iddaare, 'yes, he is'; avaru eega illa, 'he is not here now'; horage hogiddaare, 'he has gone out'; ondu nimisha, 'one moment'.

To leave word: naanu fon maadidde anta heli, 'please say that I called' (anta marks what is to be said - see the unit on joining sentences).

guide.title: Fixing a time
guide.text:
ಸಿಗು (sigu) means 'to be found, to be got' and is the everyday verb for 'meet': sigona, 'let's meet'; naale sigteeni, 'I'll see you tomorrow'.

To ask whether something is possible, use the -oke form + aaguttaa?: naale sigoke aaguttaa? 'is it possible to meet tomorrow?'. Answers: aagutte, 'yes, that works'; aagalla, 'no, I can't'.

Time expressions: eshtu gantege? 'at what time?'; hattu gantege, 'at ten'; sanje aidu gantege, 'at five in the evening'; naale beligge, 'tomorrow morning'.

'Late' is tada, or far more often the English word: letaagi, 'late (as an adverb)'; let aagutte, 'it will get late'.

Appointments use the English word: apaayintment.

examples.english: Tomorrow isn't possible; the day after is fine.

phrases.note: Put your own name in place of Ravi.
iddaare + -aa. More formal: ravi avaru iddaaraa?
Literally 'it is not being heard'. Written: kelisuttilla (ಕೇಳಿಸುತ್ತಿಲ್ಲ).
letaagi = let + aagi, 'being late'. Pure Kannada: tadavaagi (ತಡವಾಗಿ).
The usual way to close a call.
